notes: Phase 1: APPROVED. One spec defect fixed in place — AC-1 expanded a 25 KB body against a 21,162-token budget whose room_fraction ceiling is ~15.9 KB, so BR-4 would have refused the very turn AC-1 is about; AC-1 now states the expansion is admitted through BR-4's `proceed once` offer. Five warnings carried into architecture: (W-1) provenance_class values rooted/boundary are REQ-614 vocabulary while External Dependencies says None, and ContextManager holds no boundary matcher; (W-2) BR-6's 'turns <a>-<b>' names a fact ContextBlock does not carry; (W-3) AC-8's session transcript is not a repo artifact; (W-4) BR-2's second-expansion refusal is not what BR-4 governs; (W-5/info) AC-4's byte identity needs its three terms defined so the test is not vacuous.

Phase 3: APPROVED. 8/8 BRs and 9/9 ACs cited by task Verification blocks; DAG acyclic in 5 tiers; all three refusal rules (BR-1, BR-2, BR-4) carry benign_path. Firestore/REST/layering checks n/a for a Rust daemon on JSON-RPC (ADR-002); the analogous invariants (engine/surface split, single egress choke point) are respected. budget.rs and turn_loop.rs are also touched by the concurrent REQ-616/617 — textual rebase expected, no design conflict.

Phase 4 resequencing: TASK-005 (protocol events) and BR-1's refusal from TASK-006 were landed with TASK-002. Removing the in-place clamp from an anchored block without the refusal in the same commit would have shipped a daemon that silently sends over budget — worse than either end state. TASK-006's remaining items (context_compacted publish, SkillBody anchor at the model-expansion admit) still to come.

TASK-007 finding, carried to Phase 5 and the PR: ROOM_FRACTION_PERCENT = 25 (the spec's proposed starting value) measurably bites on this repo's real corpus today. The largest shipped skill body is 51 KB, not the 25 KB the spec's assumption states, and the local window is 32,768 tokens, not REQ-616's 262,144 — so /proceed is offered rather than expanded on the local tier. Three shipped behaviours move: REQ-590 AC-12's field-report turn becomes a question (a supersession REQ-618's Description explicitly wants), REQ-587's dynamic-output Stage-B refusal becomes unreachable (body + the 8,000-char output cap cannot exceed a budget a 25% body fits in), and REQ-587 BR-7's digest bypass is pre-empted on every route below ~350k tokens because digest_threshold_bytes is a larger fraction of the same budget. The last two are collateral the spec did not name. Pinned by harness::budget::tests::the_room_ceiling_and_the_digest_threshold_are_pinned_against_each_other.

Phase 5 (inline, per LESSON-629 — a 4,600-line diff is run in-context rather than dispatched): four findings, all fixed. (1) anchors_fit cloned up to three blocks — one of which can be a 25 KB body — on every loop iteration; the estimators gained iterator spellings and the anchor readers allocate nothing. (2) LESSON-565: the room check is byte-only where every other budget check is a conjunction; the crossover is now computed and written down (the two ceilings coincide at the derived 3 B/word density and separate only for denser or sparser content, in that order). (3) ContextCompacted.dropped_blocks was unbounded while the spec assumed the record fits max_record_bytes; capped at 128 rows with an omitted count, so the assumption holds by construction. (4) anchor_shape and anchor_bytes are two different measures of 'anchor bytes' — documented, and their agreement where it should hold is pinned by a test. Reflector, correctness, quality, architecture, test-coverage and security checklists all run; no Critical or unfixed Major remains.
